partners.diseaseBName: 46,XY disorder of sex development due to 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 3 deficiency
partners.mechanism_chain: ELOVL4 (HGNC:17749) —DISRUPTS→ Lipid Metabolism (GO:0006629); Lipid Metabolism (GO:0006629) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal genital development (HP:0000070); HSD17B3 (HGNC:4947) —DISRUPTS→ Androgen Biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-1908917); Androgen Biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-1908917) —PRODUCES→ Androgens (CHEBI:23775); Androgens (CHEBI:23775) —LEADS_TO→ 46,XY disorder of sex development (HP:0000079); Abnormal genital development (HP:0000070) —LEADS_TO→ 46,XY disorder of sex development (HP:0000079). Loss-of-function mutations in ELOVL4 disrupt normal lipid metabolism, which can secondarily affect steroidogenic tissues and lead to phenotypes like abnormal genital development. The convergence occurs at the level of steroidogenesis and the resulting phenotypes related to sexual development.

partners.mechanism_chain: Variant in ELOVL4 (HGNC:3029) —DISRUPTS→ ELOVL4 (HGNC:3029); ELOVL4 (HGNC:3029) —LEADS_TO→ Stargardt disease 3 (HP:0030051); ACSF3 (HGNC:27514) —DISRUPTS→ Propionyl-CoA (CHEBI:30122); Propionyl-CoA (CHEBI:30122) —DISRUPTS→ Fatty acid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-109594); Fatty acid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-109594) —LEADS_TO→ Combined malonic and methylmalonic acidemia (HP:0001349). partners.mechanism_chain: ELOVL4 (HGNC:3132) —DISRUPTS→ Very Long-Chain Fatty Acid Biosynthesis; ELOVL5 (HGNC:3133) —DISRUPTS→ Very Long-Chain Fatty Acid Biosynthesis; Very Long-Chain Fatty Acid Biosynthesis —LEADS_TO→ Spinocerebellar Ataxia (HP:0007113); Very Long-Chain Fatty Acid Biosynthesis —LEADS_TO→ Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (HP:0007174). Mutations in ELOVL4 lead to Spinocerebellar Ataxia (ALS7), while mutations in ELOVL5 lead to Spinocerebellar Ataxia type 38. Both genes are critical for the biosynthesis of very long-chain fatty acids (VLCFAs). Dysregulation of VLCFA metabolism, likely due to haploinsufficiency of either ELOVL4 or ELOVL5, disrupts neuronal homeostasis, ultimately leading to the distinct yet overlapping neurodegenerative phenotypes of spinocerebellar ataxia and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
